prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a complete, high fidelity desktop website composition for Lekton. Canvas about 1600x1100 landscape. Straight-on webpage, no device mockup, no physical scene. This is a new MINIMAL, modern, restrained public project website based on Lekton's EXISTING application theme, not a dramatic marketing redesign. The design must feel like the public entrance to the same developer documentation product. Regular Plus Jakarta Sans typography in header, headings and body. Fira Code ONLY for code. Normal-width sans headings, semibold rather than black weight. Display heading around 42 CSS pixels at desktop, not gigantic poster type. Generous useful negative space, fine dividers, small quiet controls, low contrast surface layering, crisp restrained geometry, small 6-8px component corners. Amber only for the primary button, selected nav item and the existing logo. Absolutely NO big coloured section fields, NO giant condensed letters, NO neon, NO glowing edges, NO gradients, NO decorative grids, NO three decorative feature cards, NO fake statistics, NO futuristic illustration. Real product evidence and clear how-to content do the work.
Exact webpage structure: slim 64px top navbar with small amber existing Lekton stacked-layer outline icon (three horizontal lozenge layers) and "Lekton" in normal bold 20px at left; calm nav "Product", "Setup", "Source" toward the right; tiny "EN / IT" locale control and simple sun/moon theme control. Main content fits a ~1160px container, with generous 110px whitespace before the hero. Hero left width 46%: exact heading "Documentation,\nfrom your repositories." in normal restrained sans dark/light foreground, no eyebrow. Exact supporting text "A self-hosted developer portal for Markdown, API schemas and reusable prompts. Sync content from CI, with access controls in the portal." max 3-4 lines, body 17px. Two adjacent understated rectangular buttons "Run locally" (amber filled) and "Read the source" (quiet outline). Beneath them, tiny plain text "Rust · Leptos · Axum · AGPL-3.0", not a badge.
Hero right width 54%: one impeccably composed FLAT application interface preview, gently outlined, matching the exact same website palette. No browser traffic lights, no stacked panes. The preview has its own small topbar "Lekton" and a narrow search field; left tree "Platform" with "Getting started", selected "Deployment guide", "Architecture"; "Schemas" with "Billing API"; "Prompts" with "Code review". Main document has title "Deployment guide", breadcrumb "Platform / Deployment guide", readable short example text "Build the service image, apply the configuration and verify the deployment.", then a small realistic YAML code sample with "service: billing" and "environment: staging". A small subordinate "Related" list has "Billing API · OpenAPI" and "Code review prompt". Beneath the frame explicitly label "Illustrative interface · search requires Meilisearch". Product preview has the same corners, fonts, button treatment and colours as its surrounding landing page.
Below the opening, one quiet full-width ruled horizontal workflow in the same page background, not a huge infographic: small text "Your repositories", a file description "Markdown · schemas · prompts", thin connecting arrow to a simple code label "lekton-sync", thin arrow to "Lekton", a small explanatory line "Run the sync command in CI to publish changed content." Next, an editorial two-column region at bottom of canvas, using simple typography and separators, no cards: left heading "What is included" and three clear lines "Documentation and editing", "OpenAPI, AsyncAPI and JSON Schema", "Access controls, prompts and MCP". Right heading "Run it locally" above a low-height shell block with exact commands "git clone https://github.com/dghilardi/lekton.git", "cd lekton", "docker compose up --build". Below commands text "First run builds the application. Demo authentication is for local evaluation." Small honest optional note "Search needs Meilisearch. RAG needs Qdrant, embeddings and an LLM provider." No invented customer names or performance assertions. No other wording or extra decorative sections. This is a visual composition for later semantic responsive HTML implementation, not a screenshot claimed to be the live app. LIGHT version. Match the actual default Lekton light theme values: page surface #FBFAF8, slightly elevated surface #F0EEEB, subtle dividers #E2DDD8, primary text #16181C, amber primary #A83E00 with white button text #FAF8F4. This is an almost-white warm neutral, NOT sepia or parchment. Most of the entire page is almost-white. Secondary text is neutral mid-dark grey, no sepia tint. Main heading in near-black. Fine amber details with no large amber field. Retain a decidedly contemporary product interface finish. Preview uses warm white and subtle light grey with a tiny amber selection detail.
revision: Minimal direction aligned with the default application theme; supersedes the unapproved blue concepts.
approval: User: Ok, procedi (2026-10-03). Both theme variants approved.
